answer.reason: The verses give two deeds of Ahikam himself: his errand to enquire of the LORD for the king, and his protection of Jeremiah.

clauses.english: was sent by the king to enquire of the LORD about the book of the law
kept Jeremiah from being given to the people to be put to death
clauses.quote: the hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah

doubts: 2CH 34:20 repeats the errand to Huldah and was not cited separately.
The many verses naming Gedaliah son of Ahikam concern Gedaliah, not Ahikam, so they were left out.
